newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK COURT ACQUITS MOSLEM JOURNALIST OVER ARTICLE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK COURT ACQUITS MOSLEM JOURNALIST OVER ARTICLE.

text.p: A Greek court acquitted on Thursday a Moslem journalist accused of spreading false information in a trial attended by human rights and media groups that rushed to his defence, court officials said.

Abdulhalim Dede, publisher of the weekly Turkish-language Trakyanin Sesi (Thracian Voice), was tried on charges of "spreading false information that may cause public unrest or shake people's faith in the Greek state".
"The three-member court found Mr Dede innocent after a proposal by the public prosecutor," a court official in the town of Komotini near the Greek-Turkish border, told Reuters.

Among 10 defence witnesses were members of groups saying Dede's trial was an attempt to muzzle one of the most prominent voices in Greece's 130,000-strong Moslem minority which has long been a source of tension with neighbouring Turkey.

The Greek office of the Helsinki Watch human rights group campaigned to have the charges against Dede dropped and the Foreign Press Association of Greece (FPA) sent a defence witness to Komotini in a show of solidarity.
"Our colleague Dede, who has been a stringer for Agence France Presse since 1987, has always been a very careful journalist and driven only by his passion for the truth," the FPA said in a statement.

Charges against Dede stemmed from an article he wrote in his paper, alleging that a local group of Greeks from Turkey was carrying out a campaign against the Moslem minority in Western Thrace with the connivance of local authorities.
Dede said he was charged after the group wrote a letter to the local prosecutor.
"By prosecuting me they are trying to terrorise Moslems in Western Thrace," Dede told Reuters before the trial.
Thrace's Moslem minority is at the centre of several disputes between NATO allies Greece and Turkey. Ankara insists they are Turks and that their minority rights are violated by the Greek government.
Athens says there is no such thing as an ethnic Turkish minority but a Moslem community of various ethnic backgrounds, remnants of the Ottoman empire which ruled the area until 1913.
